body: Should we use float literals instead of doubles to prevent rounding tripping `float -> double -> float`? Or is it actually useful for precision to do the multiplication in `double`s?
Also, could we mitigate the performance regression by using a possibly cheaper `CLAMP(val * scale + 0.5f, 0, scale)` instead of `std::round`? Could be an inlined helper function to deduplicate a bit.

Sounds like it could help, I asked Claude to try it and it came back with this:
```
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
  │                         Version                          │  4096²   │  1024²   │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼──────────┤
  │ Pre-PR (truncating cast, no rounding)                    │ 132.0 ms │ 6.42 ms  │                                                                                                                               
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼──────────┤                                                                                                                               
  │ PR as merged (Math::round(x * 255.0), double literals)   │ 232.3 ms │ 12.95 ms │                                                                                                                               
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────┼──────────┤                                                                                                                               
  │ With _quantize_unorm fix (float literals + x+0.5f trick) │ 132.8 ms │ 6.54 ms  │                                                                                                                               
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────┴──────────┘ 
```

Its `_quantize_unorm` helper is this:
```cpp
// Scales a normalized float channel by p_scale and rounds it to the nearest integer in [0, p_scale].
// Uses a fast round-half-up instead of a full round() call; still correct for negative inputs, since
// the CLAMP below always maps them to 0 regardless of which way they get rounded first.
template <typename T>
_FORCE_INLINE_ T _quantize_unorm(float p_value, float p_scale) {
       return T(CLAMP(p_value * p_scale + 0.5f, 0.0f, p_scale));
}
```
I updated the PR to use the simpler (+ 0.5f) rounding, the errors are pretty much the same as the `Math::round()` version and the performance differs only by an extremely small margin

I'd suggest extracting to a helper function so we can deduplicate that redundant operation somewhat.

I think `0` and `15` should also be float literals so that `CLAMP` doesn't end up doing implicit conversions to compare `float` and `int` (though I don't know if that has any performance implications).

Thank you for the suggestions! I'll update the measurements soon
